summary: Genuinely mutual Dutch-party NDA on English law, but with a one-way feedback IP assignment to Vanderberg, a one-way publicity right, a 48-hour no-exception return period, one-way assignment, and a heightened carve-out evidence standard.

findings.quote: "Disclosing Party" means the Party, or an Affiliate of such Party, that discloses, transmits, or makes available Proprietary Materials to the Receiving Party
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined by role so either Party can be either, and clause 2 binds the Receiving Party equally.

findings.quote: that is marked or identified as confidential or proprietary, or that reasonably ought to be understood as confidential given the nature of the information or the circumstances attending its disclosure.
findings.why: Definition covers marked or reasonably confidential information disclosed by either Party, though it does not expressly mention derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: other than strictly in furtherance of the Authorized Purpose.
findings.why: Use is limited to the Authorized Purpose, a prospective commercial collaboration between the Parties.

findings.quote: that the Receiving Party can convincingly prove by contemporaneous written records:
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present, but the proof standard of 'convincingly prove by contemporaneous written records' is stricter than the accepted 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence'.
findings.draft_redline: that the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are content with the four standard exclusions but would prefer the evidential standard to be written records or reasonable evidence, rather than contemporaneous records proved convincingly.

findings.quote: that Party's and its Affiliates' respective directors, managing directors (bestuurders), officers, employees, independent contractors, professional legal counsel, accountants, auditors, and financial advisors.
findings.why: Representatives cover employees, advisers, auditors and Affiliates on a need-to-know basis with liability under 2.4, but insurers are not listed and no ACCEPTABLE line clearly fits.
findings.draft_redline: "Representatives" means, with respect to a Party, that Party's and its Affiliates' respective directors, officers, employees, independent contractors, professional advisers, accountants, auditors and insurers.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like insurers to be included among permitted recipients; the rest of the Representatives definition works for us.

findings.quote: immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing of such legal requirement, to the extent legally permissible
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice is qualified by legal permissibility and cooperation is at the Disclosing Party's sole expense.
findings.fallback_cited: Notice 'where lawful' and cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: Within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt of a written notice from the Disclosing Party requesting the return or destruction of Proprietary Materials
findings.why: A 48-hour return or destruction period is well under the 5 Business Day minimum.
findings.draft_redline: Within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of a written notice from the Disclosing Party requesting the return or destruction of Proprietary Materials, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy them.
findings.note_to_counterparty: A 48-hour deadline is not practicable for us; we propose ten Business Days for return or destruction.

findings.quote: containing or reflecting any Proprietary Materials, without exception
findings.why: Destruction applies 'without exception', with no carve-out for automated backups or copies required to be retained by law, which stay confidential.
findings.draft_redline: The Receiving Party may retain copies held in automated electronic backups or required to be retained by law or regulation, provided such copies remain subject to this Agreement.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to be able to keep automated backup copies and copies we are legally required to retain; these will remain confidential under the Agreement.

findings.quote: No right, license, title, or interest in or to any Intellectual Property Rights of the Disclosing Party is granted, assigned, or transferred to the Receiving Party by implication, estoppel, or otherwise
findings.why: Proprietary Materials and IP remain with the Disclosing Party and the only licence is to evaluate for the Authorized Purpose (clauses 5.1 and 5.2).

findings.quote: all Intellectual Property Rights in such modifications, adaptations, improvements, derivative works, and feedback shall vest exclusively in Vanderberg upon creation, and Halyard hereby assigns to Vanderberg
findings.why: Halyard assigns IP in improvements, derivatives and feedback to Vanderberg only, which could capture Halyard's own product information.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 5.3. Each Party retains ownership of its own Intellectual Property Rights, including in any modifications, improvements or feedback relating to its own software, technology or Proprietary Materials, and no licence is granted other than for the Authorized Purpose.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We cannot agree to assign IP in feedback or improvements to one Party only. We propose deleting clause 5.3 so that each Party keeps its own IP.

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation, express, statutory, or implied, regarding the accuracy, sufficiency, completeness, or fitness for any purpose of any Proprietary Materials
findings.why: Information is provided 'as is' with a mutual disclaimer of warranty and no Halyard warranty on accuracy.

findings.quote: neither Party shall issue any formal press release or public statement concerning this Agreement or the commercial discussions between the Parties without the prior written approval of the other Party.
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction with a legal-requirement exception, subject to the carve-out in 7.2.

findings.quote: Vanderberg shall be entitled to reference Halyard by name, trade name, and company logo in Vanderberg's client lists, marketing collaterals, commercial pitch decks, and website disclosures
findings.why: Vanderberg alone may use Halyard's name and logo and announce the discussions without consent.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to agree to one-way use of our name and logo; please delete clause 7.2 so the mutual consent requirement in 7.1 applies to both Parties.

findings.quote: business plans, customer data, and documentation disclosed or made accessible
findings.why: The definition expressly contemplates 'customer data' being disclosed, yet the NDA has no data protection terms or DPA commitment.
findings.draft_redline: Neither Party shall disclose personal data to the other under this Agreement other than business contact details. Any other sharing of personal data requires a prior separate data processing or sharing agreement and compliance by both Parties with UK GDPR and EU GDPR.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to add a short clause that no personal data beyond business contact details is shared without a separate data processing agreement.

findings.quote: initial term of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon thirty (30) calendar days' written notice
findings.why: Term is two years with 30 days' notice to terminate, as preferred.

findings.quote: shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years
findings.why: Five-year survival is within the accepted 2 to 5 year range, though there is no separate Trade Secret protection.

findings.quote: the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and any other provisional remedies or equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction, without the necessity of posting a bond or other security.
findings.why: Equitable relief is available to the Disclosing Party (either Party) on an 'entitled to seek' basis with no bond.
findings.fallback_cited: 'Entitled to seek' rather than 'entitled to'; no requirement to post a bond.

findings.quote: the laws of England and Wales. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales
findings.why: English law with exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts, as preferred.

findings.quote: provided, however, that Vanderberg may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate upon written notice to Halyard.
findings.why: Only Vanderberg may assign to an Affiliate on notice while Halyard needs consent.
findings.draft_redline: provided, however, that either Party may assign this Agreement to a member of its Group or a successor to its business upon written notice to the other Party.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the right to assign to an affiliate on notice to apply to both Parties equally.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party shall refrain from disassembling, decompiling, reverse engineering, decrypting
findings.why: Mutual prohibition on reverse engineering software and prototypes.

findings.quote: This Agreement constitutes the complete and exclusive understanding and agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof
findings.why: Customary entire-agreement clause that does not exclude liability for fraud; third-party rights are excluded in 10.6.
